answer: Sybil resistance by admission auction with burned marginal bids. Each epoch one global sealed-bid auction admits only K=64 new identities: bids lock in the vault, losing marginal bids burn like an ember, slot i pays the (K+i)-th rejected bid. Validators refuse signatures from keys without a paid slot. Since all demand clears in one market, an attacker's n own bids push the clearing price up: marginal cost grows at least linearly in n. Bids stay vault-locked, non-transferable while active, barring rented, split, or pre-farmed identities; the saffron log audits admissions.
